fatal_errors: The proposed Q235/FLiBe system does not reconstruct the target SS316L substrate, AlCoCrFeNi atmospheric-plasma-sprayed coating, or post-deposition annealing study.
It omits the governing 550 °C annealing condition and the comparison with as-sprayed and uncoated SS316L references.
The 700 °C, 1000 h FLiBe exposure is unrelated to the target electrochemical H2SO4 testing and 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot corrosion.
The cited Mn-dissolution mechanism was observed in a bulk Mn-containing HEA that performed worse than 316H; it does not support improved performance of an unspecified HEA coating on Q235.
The causal statement is internally inconsistent: the hypothesis says Cr retention discourages Mn dissolution, whereas the cited evidence says Mn dissolution appears to discourage Cr dissolution.

The experiment measures only overall corrosion rate and microstructure, so it cannot isolate whether Mn dissolution, Cr retention, a Cr-rich precipitate, coating defects, or substrate shielding governs performance.
explanation: The response has the broad idea of comparing HEA-coated and uncoated steel under high-temperature salt exposure, but nearly every target-specific element is absent. It does not specify AlCoCrFeNi, APS deposition, coating thickness, annealing series, the 550 °C optimum, passive Al/Cr-rich oxides, or the target electrochemical and cyclic hot-corrosion conditions. Its evidence is valid for phase instability and selective Mn dissolution in a bulk Cr-Mn-Fe-Ni HEA exposed to FLiBe, but the response extrapolates that observation to an unspecified coating on Q235 without establishing compositional or mechanistic applicability. A valid causal test would require controlled coating composition and annealing, measurements of Mn and Cr flux into the salt, depth-resolved composition and phase analysis, and coating-defect/scale characterization rather than corrosion rate alone.
